title: Proposed collaboration on NSF-related epileptic encephalopathy

sentences.text: Exploring a research collaboration on NSF-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
We are writing to [the patient organisation]; to be honest, our atlas lists no patient organisation for this condition, so we would be grateful to hear who best serves these families.
This condition is linked to a dominant-negative effect, where the altered protein blocks the working one.
That view rests on a single report and a fruit fly eye assay, so it remains uncertain.
Our atlas lists no registry, natural history study or trial for this condition.
We would like to explore a jointly designed study on NSF-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, shaped with your community from the start: [study question], [design], [sites].
Any participation would follow informed consent and ethics approval, and we would share what we learn with your community.

sections.heading: What we would ask of you

sentences.text: Would you be open to a conversation about whether this idea is useful to the families you serve?
If so, we would value your view on how your community, registry or natural history work could take part, with proper consent and ethics approval.
We are not asking for any personal information about patients or families.
Could we arrange a short call at a time that suits you, perhaps [proposed dates]?
With thanks and warm regards, [researcher name], [institution].
